# Representative Mission fixture review

These are synthetic adaptations for human review and the
`representative_mission_fixtures` integration tests. They do not execute or
mutate their inspiration roadmaps, source stores, or live Mission data.

## Review entries

| Corpus | Source map | API-generated entry | Review focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Documentation workflow — 4 waypoints | [Source map](source-maps/documentation-workflow.md) | [Generated README](generated/documentation-workflow/generated/README.md), [ROADMAP](generated/documentation-workflow/generated/ROADMAP.md), [waypoint map](generated/documentation-workflow/generated/waypoints/README.md) | Distinct contract, health-check, code-map, and human semantic-review objectives; includes synthetic operator-result evidence. |
| Mission integration — 9 waypoints | [Source map](source-maps/mission-integration.md) | [Generated README](generated/mission-integration/generated/README.md), [ROADMAP](generated/mission-integration/generated/ROADMAP.md), [waypoint map](generated/mission-integration/generated/waypoints/README.md) | Native Mission boundaries, reference-only synthetic links, typed Parts, three complete revisions, changed REQUEST, preserved continuations, archived states, and a separately recorded synthetic reaction. |
| Ticket reliability and migration — 17 waypoints | [Source map](source-maps/ticket-reliability.md) | [Generated README](generated/ticket-reliability/generated/README.md), [ROADMAP](generated/ticket-reliability/generated/ROADMAP.md), [waypoint map](generated/ticket-reliability/generated/waypoints/README.md) | Completed fixture work, blocked migration apply, pending transport work, and the explicit separate-approval boundary. |

Every entry links its generated Parts below `generated/<corpus>/generated/waypoints/`.
The sibling `accepted.json`, `artifact-provenance.json`, `output-contract.json`,
`history/`, and `REQUEST.md` files are also generated by Mission APIs and are
part of exact-byte tests. No generated file is hand-authored or normalized.

## Synthetic-data boundaries

- `authoring/` contains deterministic native-v2 or typed-v3 API inputs. Stable
  IDs are fixture-only. `generated/` is the actual full Mission-store output
  created by the final Mission APIs.
- Ticket, Specification, criterion, and Test/evidence references resolve only
  against synthetic stores created beneath each isolated temporary workspace.
  At least one documentation waypoint has no Ticket or foreign references.
- Mission's validator requires immediate predecessor checkpoints for ordered
  waypoints. The native fixture records that API-defined rendering order;
  typed publication applies the same order contract. These links are fixture
  adaptations, not claims that the source roadmaps had those prerequisites.
  No cross-Mission dependency is introduced.
- Expected outcomes, alternatives, acceptable handling, statuses, validation
  receipts, and reactions are fixture-authored. They are not original
  requester approvals, human review, authentication, or source execution.
  The documentation operator result is a synthetic API-recorded example.
- In the Ticket example, the first fifteen fixture waypoints are completed,
  the live-migration waypoint is blocked, and transport integration is
  pending. The blocked boundary remains unresolved in the example; no apply,
  verification, or undo is performed.

## Regeneration and verification

From the meta-workspace root, explicitly regenerate committed review output:

```text
cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools/Cargo.toml --locked -p mission-api --test representative_mission_fixtures regenerate_reviewable_outputs -- --ignored --exact
```

The ignored generator reads the committed authoring inputs, creates fresh
temporary workspace and synthetic entity stores under the Mission API crate,
publishes through Mission APIs, and copies the complete API-owned Mission
trees into `generated/`. It does not strip timestamps, paths, fields, archives,
or event data. Normal tests never rewrite these fixtures:

```text
cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools/Cargo.toml --locked -p mission-api --test representative_mission_fixtures
```

That test generates the same authoring inputs in fresh roots and byte-compares
the entire Mission trees, then verifies same-store read-back, generated-file
checks, whole-state contracts and history. It also checks controlled missing
reference, output drift, and malformed-plan failures without rewriting
accepted state.

## Archive-link observation

The current `generated/HISTORY.md` links resolve from the published
`generated/` directory to the complete `history/states/revision-N/` archives.
Each archive also preserves its own byte-identical `generated/HISTORY.md`;
the relative links in that frozen archived copy do not resolve from inside
the archive's nested `generated/` directory. The whole-state contract
verification confirms those archived bytes remain intact. The harness does
not rewrite archived output to make context-sensitive links appear valid.
